current.text: He re-signed with Minnesota on a minimum contract.
He is in Minnesota's 10-man rotation at about 15 minutes per game.
Experts call him a bench scoring option who can put up numbers. They also say a steady role is hard to find, so he is a roll of the dice.
He adds guard depth and is seen as good enough to fill in when a starter is out.
Minnesota's bench is thin. It has little scoring punch and no ball handlers.
Donte DiVincenzo will miss most of the season and Mike Conley is gone. Dosunmu, Shannon and Green are the other guards competing for backcourt minutes.
With the season ending March 28, Minnesota plays 4, 2 and 4 games in the fantasy playoff weeks, so the semifinal week has only two games. The team has the league minimum of 13 back-to-backs.
Ben expects Minnesota to win 53 games, and the team is not expected to rest players to tank.

durable.text: He is a bench scoring guard whose value depends on how many minutes he gets.

note: He is a waiver player for us. Yahoo ranks him 251 and ESPN 283, both value him at 0 USD, and our league did not draft him last season. In about 15 bench minutes he gives a thin line: some threes and low turnovers (0.8 per game projected), but little else. Early in the season, check whether Minnesota's thin bench, which has no ball handlers, pushes his minutes above 15, and whether an injury to Ball or Edwards opens starts for him. Even then, the two-game semifinal week caps his playoff use.
